summary: Wired the pure match, claim and intel modules into MatchRoom so a private match can be played and won end to end. Lobby: the host starts with 2 or more players (PRIVATE_MIN_PLAYERS is the single source). Late joiners are refused at admission ('That match has already started'). Ready countdown, then control start: every ship gets the encounter rules' spawn protection, the claim config's deadline is set (the timer and the deadline come from one config), and intel starts. Tick order: encounters -> ledger holds -> claim -> match flow -> intel reveals. Reveals go only to their recipients: the sector to everyone, the exact route only to a full-set holder, route-inactive on a lost type, and the minute-20 and minute-28 broadcasts. Claim channel with interrupts; endings: claim, deadline, abandoned, aborted (a world tick that throws is caught as a fault). Results come from ledger diffs and settled duels. One node:crypto master secret per match, with an HMAC-SHA-256 seed per system (world, ledger, final-socket, intel, duel:n; ruins and fruit reserved); the ledger seed now uses it. Protocol v7 (start-match, start-refused, reveal). Test-only settings (off by default, not read by main.ts): timings, a pinned final-socket secret, an injected master secret, and testHooks (injectFault, pauseAfterTick/resumeWorld). Web: lobby panel, clock bar with the timer and sector, reveal banners and log, compass, treasure circle and minimap mark, claim panel with its risk line, rival-claim warning, and a results screen with 'Back to lobby'. Carry-forwards: event.repeat ignored in the theft-choice keys, the Phaser.AUTO comment fixed, the per-tick invariant asserted in seaDuelHarness, and the dock-reuse branch of sourceSites unit-tested. Docs updated: architecture, README, encounters, objectives. Checks I ran myself: npm ci; npm run typecheck (0 errors); npm run test:unit (53 files, 1230 tests); npm run test:integration (16 files, 89 tests, 157 s); npm run build (smoke passed); the full Playwright suite (10 passed), then with the JSON reporter on every spec plus check-report (all 9 scenarios ok).
open_assumptions: Public state, the lobby and the results name players by seat ('Player N', join order), not by session id, so a ship's id still first reaches a client when that ship comes into sight (the existing visibility raw-frame test requires this).
Cancelled duels (both fighters gone, or cut off by the match's end) count as neither won, lost nor drawn in the results; settled wins and draws do.
The ledger's holds run between the encounters and the claim in each tick (encounters -> holds -> claim -> match -> intel).
The intel view includes a player who left while an unsettled duel still reserves their rubbings, at their exit position; otherwise stepIntel would throw and abort the match.
privateMatch.minPlayers (1) in packages/content/src/rules.ts is stale. It is not read (the room uses PRIVATE_MIN_PLAYERS = 2) and is reported here for a later content cleanup (not owned).
Browser server test-only settings: a 3 s ready countdown, 1 s of departure protection, a 10-minute match, and final-socket secret 3 (the south-east islet).
untested: The claim's 'ineligible' reset during a live channel cannot happen through the room (a type is lost only through a duel, whose reservation resets the channel first). It is covered by the pure claim module; the integration test covers 'cannot restart after losing a type'.
The 'waiting' claim state (a second eligible claimer while another channels) and the rival-claim warning in a browser (the warning is unit-tested only).
An aborted ending from a real, non-injected exception (only the injected fault hook is tested).
A disconnect or seat expiry during the lobby or the ready countdown, and reconnecting into those phases.
verify_yourself: That naming players by seat ('Player 1 (you, host)') in the lobby and on the results screen, rather than by session id or a display name, is acceptable until player names exist.
